findings.highlight: The heat radiating from my shoulder
findings.evidenceJa: 肩の付け根から侵入する熱
findings.governingReading: Heat invades Shirou through the base of his shoulder.
findings.explanation: “Radiating from” reverses the inward motion and makes the shoulder a source of heat.

findings.evidenceJa: 極小の蟲
findings.governingReading: The invasive heat resembles tiny insects eating his cells.
findings.explanation: The English adds a plague-scale collective judgment.

findings.highlight: realize that I’ve been scorched black
findings.evidenceJa: 気を抜けばいつのまにか真っ黒焦げになっている
findings.governingReading: If his attention lapses, he imagines he will find himself charred black before he knows it.
findings.explanation: The English turns a conditional threat into completed injury and invents a moment of realization.

findings.evidenceJa: ジリジリとゴウゴウと
findings.governingReading: The heat advances with simmering and roaring sound-symbolic force.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the paired sensory sounds with generic manner adverbs.

findings.highlight: allowing the ants to flood into my body
findings.evidenceJa: 無遠慮に体の中に入ってきた
findings.governingReading: The imagined insects enter his body with invasive, unrestrained impertinence.
findings.explanation: The English adds flooding but removes the personified lack of restraint.

findings.highlight: the entrancethe hole to let them out
findings.evidenceJa: 連中を外に出すべき穴
findings.governingReading: The opening that should let the intruders back out is sealed with foreign flesh.
findings.explanation: The English contains a fused draft fragment that breaks the sentence.

findings.highlight: changing to something I don’t know
findings.evidenceJa: 得体の知れないモノに変わっていく
findings.governingReading: He feels himself changing into something whose nature cannot be grasped.
findings.explanation: The English reduces ontological alienness to lack of acquaintance.

findings.evidenceJa: 知るはずのない知識
findings.governingReading: Knowledge he could not possibly possess enters him.
findings.explanation: “Shouldn’t have” suggests prohibition or moral impropriety rather than impossibility.

findings.evidenceJa: 鍛冶を生業とする英霊
findings.governingReading: He identifies Archer as a Heroic Spirit whose trade was smithing.
findings.explanation: The English noun pile is malformed and obscures the occupational parallel.

findings.highlight: duplicates everything he sees and understands
findings.evidenceJa: いくらでも複製する
findings.governingReading: He can reproduce any number of things he has seen and understood.
findings.explanation: The English retains the eligibility condition but drops the unlimited quantity.

findings.highlight: an image in the caster’s mind
findings.evidenceJa: 術者の創造理念
findings.governingReading: Projection uses the practitioner’s creative conception or governing ideal to reproduce the genuine work.
findings.explanation: The English reduces a structured creative principle to a generic mental picture.

findings.evidenceJa: それを使いこなせ
findings.governingReading: The invading knowledge demands that Shirou master and wield Projection fully.
findings.explanation: “Manage” weakens command of the technique and is unnatural here.

findings.highlight: Cutting corners like this will destroy my body
findings.evidenceJa: そんな近道は必ずこの身を破滅させる
findings.governingReading: Such a shortcut will certainly destroy his embodied self.
findings.explanation: The English narrows this self/body to the physical body and drops certainty.

findings.evidenceJa: そんな他所のモノを見せ付けられても
findings.governingReading: He protests that having an alien person’s material forced before him will not let him learn or master it.
findings.explanation: The English prematurely labels the foreign material a single ability and drops its imposed presentation.

findings.highlight: You can’t put time out of order
findings.evidenceJa: 時間を狂わせてはいけない
findings.governingReading: His overloaded protest says that time must not be distorted.
findings.explanation: The English changes a prohibition against violating time into second-person inability.

findings.evidenceJa: 秩序を乱してはいけない
findings.governingReading: He insists that order must not be disturbed.
findings.explanation: “Destroy the regularity” is non-English and changes order into regularity.

findings.evidenceJa: はた、と目が合う
findings.governingReading: Shirou suddenly finds his eyes meeting Illya’s.
findings.explanation: The English omits the abrupt beat.

findings.evidenceJa: 本当に嬉しい
findings.governingReading: He is genuinely glad that Illya is safe despite not understanding the situation.
findings.explanation: The English drops the emphatic sincerity.

findings.highlight: Hugging me, she buries her face in my chest
findings.evidenceJa: ばふ、と頭からこっちの胸に飛び込んできて
findings.governingReading: Illya flies headfirst into his chest with a soft impact.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her full rushing action and its sound with a settled hug.

findings.evidenceJa: “よかった”を繰り返す
findings.governingReading: Illya repeatedly says that she is glad he survived and woke.
findings.explanation: The English hides the specific relief she cannot stop voicing.

findings.highlight: I can’t do anything if she’s crying like this
findings.evidenceJa: 泣きつかれたら大人しくしているしかない
findings.governingReading: With Illya clinging to him in tears, Shirou feels he can only stay quietly still.
findings.explanation: The English drops her clinging and his specific response.

findings.highlight: I’ll make him put on another one
findings.evidenceJa: すぐ代わりの物をつけさせる
findings.governingReading: Illya offers to have a replacement fitted immediately if anything feels wrong.
findings.explanation: The English invents a male operator and makes the referent sound like clothing.

findings.evidenceJa: してくれ、と言いかけて
findings.governingReading: Shirou is cut off just as he begins to ask Illya for an explanation.
findings.explanation: The English makes the speech already ongoing and deletes what he was about to request.

findings.evidenceJa: 左腕を抑えつける
findings.governingReading: Illya tells Shirou to pin down or restrain the left arm instead of merely enduring the pain.
findings.explanation: “Repress” is an abstract psychological verb and obscures the physical instruction.

findings.highlight: if I know the origin of the pain
findings.evidenceJa: 異物がなんであるか判れば
findings.governingReading: Control becomes possible once Shirou identifies what the foreign element is.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the identity of the foreign substance with the pain’s origin.

findings.evidenceJa: だぼだぼの病人服
findings.governingReading: He has been dressed in baggy patient’s clothing.
findings.explanation: “Big hospital clothes” is unnatural and loses the garment’s looseness and patient-specific role.

findings.evidenceJa: シロウと一緒に外に出る
findings.governingReading: Illya insists she will go outside together with Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes going outside into leaving, weakening the physical and custodial claim.

findings.evidenceJa: あっさりと俺を裸にした
findings.governingReading: Kirei casually unfastens the restraint belts and strips Shirou naked.
findings.explanation: The English sanitizes the completed exposure into removing unspecified coverings.

findings.evidenceJa: 何重にも巻かれた布
findings.governingReading: The alien arm is perceptible even through cloth wound around it in many layers.
findings.explanation: The English drops the multiple heavy layers of wrapping.

findings.highlight: My left arm is not part of my body
findings.evidenceJa: いま左腕になっているものは、自分以外の何か
findings.governingReading: What now serves as Shirou’s left arm is something belonging to or originating from someone other than himself.
findings.explanation: The English says it is not part of his body, contradicting Kirei’s later explanation that it has become his flesh.

findings.highlight: attached by opposing the natural Providence
findings.evidenceJa: 自然の摂理を押し曲げてまで取り付けた
findings.governingReading: The foreign object was attached only by bending the order of nature.
findings.explanation: The English is malformed, capitalizes “Providence,” and turns bending natural law into opposing it.

findings.evidenceJa: アーチャー本人の意思を尊重し
findings.governingReading: Kirei respected Archer’s own conscious will in performing the transplant.
findings.explanation: “Wish” narrows deliberate volition and weakens the emphasis on Archer personally choosing.

findings.evidenceJa: アーチャーが、消滅した
findings.governingReading: Archer has vanished from the world after enduring through the completed transplant.
findings.explanation: “Eliminated” suggests that another party defeated or removed him.

findings.highlight: a part of a heroic spirit
findings.evidenceJa: 現世に受肉させている英霊の肉
findings.governingReading: Archer’s severed flesh is incarnated and sustained in the present world by Shirou’s magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English keeps persistence but omits incarnation as flesh.

findings.evidenceJa: おまえもアーチャーも長くはなかった
findings.governingReading: Neither Shirou nor Archer had long to live in their respective conditions.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the limited remaining duration.

findings.evidenceJa: 唯一無事な肉体を提供する
findings.governingReading: Archer offers the one intact portion of his body that can replace Shirou’s loss.
findings.explanation: The English implies he donates his whole body.

findings.highlight: divine mysteries that cannot be handled with magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術では扱えない神秘
findings.governingReading: Soul resurrection and restoration belong to mystery outside ordinary magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English adds divinity, changing Fate’s technical category into a religious one.

findings.evidenceJa: 形だけ成功した後で
findings.governingReading: Kirei expected the joining to succeed only in outward form before shock killed Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Succeeded in shape” is malformed and obscures the distinction between physical joining and soul restoration.

findings.highlight: he would pull through if the connection was made
findings.evidenceJa: この二人なら、繋がりさえすれば持ち直す
findings.governingReading: Illya identifies Shirou and Archer as a special pair whose connection permits recovery.
findings.explanation: The English changes the pair into a singular “he,” obscuring reciprocal compatibility.

findings.evidenceJa: なんとなく悲しそうに
findings.governingReading: Illya averts and shifts her gaze with an impression of vague sadness.
findings.explanation: The English states sadness directly and drops its indistinct quality.

findings.highlight: Even twin brothers would not look this alike
findings.evidenceJa: 双子でもここまで瓜二つではなかろう
findings.governingReading: Their compatibility is so nearly identical that even twins would not match this closely.
findings.explanation: The English makes the comparison about visible appearance and adds male gender.

findings.evidenceJa: 左腕に力を入れてみた
findings.governingReading: Shirou tries to put strength into the left arm to test Kirei’s claim.
findings.explanation: “Flex” implies successful movement immediately before the text establishes that the arm cannot move.

findings.evidenceJa: ただの塊
findings.governingReading: The arm is merely an insensate mass despite being attached.
findings.explanation: The English invents dead flesh, contradicting the explanation that Shirou’s energy sustains it as his living body.

findings.evidenceJa: 麻痺した腕
findings.governingReading: The sensation resembles an arm numbed after its circulation is cut off.
findings.explanation: The English narrows the affected limb from arm to hand.

findings.evidenceJa: ただの鉄くれ
findings.governingReading: The left arm feels like a mere lump of iron.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes iron into unspecified metal.

findings.evidenceJa: ブリキになった人間
findings.governingReading: Shirou imagines the disability of a person whose body had become tin.
findings.explanation: “Tin man” introduces a stock literary figure absent from the source.

findings.evidenceJa: こんな不自由さ
findings.governingReading: He imagines this degree of physical incapacity and lack of freedom.
findings.explanation: “Constricted” describes tightness rather than disability.

findings.highlight: It shall familiarize with your body
findings.evidenceJa: 数日経てば馴染む
findings.governingReading: Kirei predicts that the joined arm will adapt to Shirou after several days.
findings.explanation: The English uses “familiarize” in an ungrammatical intransitive construction.

findings.highlight: heal well enough to give you no trouble
findings.evidenceJa: 通常の生活をこなせるほどには回復
findings.governingReading: Kirei predicts recovery sufficient to carry out ordinary daily life.
findings.explanation: The English overstates functional sufficiency as freedom from trouble.

findings.highlight: it will swallow you if you use it
findings.evidenceJa: 使えばおまえとて巻き込まれよう
findings.governingReading: If Shirou uses the weaponlike arm, he too will be caught up in its power and consequences.
findings.explanation: The English prematurely imports a swallowing metaphor into the technical warning.

findings.evidenceJa: 内部から崩壊する
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s body will collapse from within when Archer’s circuits activate.
findings.explanation: The English drops the direction and visceral mechanism.

findings.highlight: Pain will assail your arm as it reacts and tries to activate
findings.evidenceJa: その度に左腕には痛みと、起動しようとする反動
findings.governingReading: Each ordinary circulation of magical energy brings pain and a recoil toward activation in the left arm.
findings.explanation: The English omits the repeated trigger and blurs recoil into a generic reaction.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔力殺しの聖骸布
findings.governingReading: The shroud suppresses magical energy itself, which is why it restrains activation and invasion.
findings.explanation: The English gives only a name and drops the stated functional property.

findings.highlight: the infringement from your left arm
findings.evidenceJa: 左腕からの侵食
findings.governingReading: The shroud partly suppresses the arm’s physical and magical encroachment into Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Infringement” is a legal or rights term and fails to express invasive consumption.

findings.evidenceJa: 一人前になって
findings.governingReading: Shirou must become a fully fledged magus capable of governing the arm.
findings.explanation: “Master magus” overstates the required rank and risks confusion with Master terminology.

findings.evidenceJa: 成れずに自滅するか
findings.governingReading: If he fails to mature enough, the imbalance will make him destroy himself.
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s self-destruction and makes him a passive victim.

findings.evidenceJa: 助かった命を放棄する
findings.governingReading: Complaining would amount to throwing away the life the transplant rescued.
findings.explanation: The English changes repudiation of a specifically saved life into a general absence of desire to live.

findings.evidenceJa: 減らず口が言える
findings.governingReading: Kirei treats Shirou’s irrepressible cheek and banter as proof he need not worry.
findings.explanation: The English removes the characterization of Shirou’s remark as impertinent backtalk.

findings.highlight: I can’t move my left hand
findings.evidenceJa: 左腕は動かない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot move the transplanted left arm.
findings.explanation: The English again narrows arm-wide immobility to the hand.

findings.highlight: I just drape it over my shoulder
findings.evidenceJa: とりあえず羽織っただけ
findings.governingReading: Because the arm cannot move, Shirou merely drapes the jacket around himself without properly putting it on.
findings.explanation: The English invents a single-shoulder placement.

findings.evidenceJa: いつのまにか夜になっていた
findings.governingReading: Night has fallen without Shirou noticing while he was unconscious and treated.
findings.explanation: The English conveys lateness but drops the unnoticed transition.

findings.evidenceJa: せいぜいうまく立ち回れ
findings.governingReading: Kirei tells Shirou to maneuver as skillfully as he can with the choice and danger in mind.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the tactical conduct and reduces it to generic encouragement.

findings.evidenceJa: 命を担保にされかねない
findings.governingReading: Rin warns that further debt could put a life—most immediately her own—up as collateral.
findings.explanation: The English makes the threatened life plural and distributes the risk to the whole group.

findings.highlight: The Holy Grail War is a failure
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯戦争も破綻している
findings.governingReading: Kirei says the Grail War’s operative structure has broken down under the current conditions.
findings.explanation: The English evaluates the war as unsuccessful instead of describing institutional collapse.

findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂は黙り込む
findings.governingReading: Rin falls silent at Kirei’s argument.
findings.explanation: The English uses an unnatural literal phrase that can imply physically closing her mouth.

findings.evidenceJa: 残った二人
findings.governingReading: The two remaining Masters with Servants would ordinarily fight.
findings.explanation: “Standing” adds a survival or tournament implication absent from the source.

findings.evidenceJa: 決まっているようなもの
findings.governingReading: Under this reasoning, the outcome is effectively as good as decided.
findings.explanation: The English turns a qualified practical conclusion into completed finality.

findings.highlight: There is no benefit to kill Zouken
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐臓硯を倒したところで、おまえたちに益はない
findings.governingReading: Even defeating Zouken would bring them no benefit under Kirei’s Grail calculus.
findings.explanation: “No benefit to kill” is malformed English and weakens the concessive premise.

findings.evidenceJa: 屋敷に立て篭もり
findings.governingReading: Kirei recommends barricading themselves inside the mansion until the war ends.
findings.explanation: The English removes the defensive fortification.

findings.evidenceJa: 正しい選択
findings.governingReading: Kirei presents withdrawal as the correct course.
findings.explanation: The English softens categorical correctness into prudent advice.

findings.highlight: one other who shamelessly stayed on the battlefield
findings.evidenceJa: のこのこ死地に赴いた者
findings.governingReading: Kirei needles Rin by recalling someone who blithely went out to a place of death after losing his Servant.
findings.explanation: The English changes movement into continued presence, death ground into a battlefield, and foolish nonchalance into shame.

findings.evidenceJa: 白旗はあげられない
findings.governingReading: Kirei says she cannot easily raise the white flag.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the surrender image.

findings.evidenceJa: 顔を背けてそっぽを向く
findings.governingReading: Rin emphatically turns her face aside and looks away in a huff.
findings.explanation: The English flattens the doubled gesture and attitude.

findings.highlight: she or Sakura has to win
findings.evidenceJa: どうせ勝つ人間が出るのなら
findings.governingReading: If someone is going to emerge victorious anyway, Rin means it should be herself or Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English drops the premise and changes preference into necessity.

findings.highlight: is still wanting to save Sakura, her younger sister
findings.evidenceJa: なんだかんだ言って妹である桜を助けたがっている
findings.governingReading: Whatever Rin says or how she frames it, Shirou reads her as wanting to save her younger sister.
findings.explanation: The English retains the motive but removes the tension between her words and concealed concern.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺だって目的はある
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he too has a definite purpose for continuing.
findings.explanation: The English makes the purpose plural and less focused.

findings.highlight: Matou Zouken is a weak person
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐臓硯は小物
findings.governingReading: Kirei calls Zouken a petty or small-caliber villain despite the hopeless power disparity.
findings.explanation: “Weak person” changes contempt for his caliber into generic weakness.

findings.highlight: I am sure you can devise some plan
findings.evidenceJa: 何らかの策はあるだろう
findings.governingReading: Kirei reasons that there may be some stratagem against a petty opponent.
findings.explanation: The English invents confidence that Shirou and Rin themselves can devise one.

findings.highlight: We look at each other silently
findings.evidenceJa: つい、お互い無言で見詰め合った
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Rin find themselves looking at each other without meaning to.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the involuntary beat that exposes their shared lack of a plan.

findings.highlight: we are not asking for protection here
findings.evidenceJa: 保護を受けない元マスター
findings.governingReading: Kirei has no reason to shelter former Masters who are not under formal protection.
findings.explanation: The English changes status and custody into a voluntary refusal to ask.

findings.highlight: I don’t mind, but I have to refuse
findings.evidenceJa: いいけど、行かない
findings.governingReading: Illya says the invitation itself is acceptable, but she will not go because Sakura is there.
findings.explanation: “Have to refuse” invents external compulsion before her reason is disclosed.

findings.highlight: I stare at Tohsaka because I don’t understand
findings.evidenceJa: 視線だけで遠坂に問いただす
findings.governingReading: Shirou uses only his gaze to press Rin for an explanation.
findings.explanation: The English removes the nonverbal question and makes the gaze merely a symptom of confusion.

findings.highlight: she looks like she doesn’t want to interfere
findings.evidenceJa: こっちに振るなって顔
findings.governingReading: Rin’s face tells Shirou not to hand the awkward question over to her.
findings.explanation: The English changes refusal to be put on the spot into a general wish not to interfere.

findings.highlight: Even if she goes back to her castle
findings.evidenceJa: このまま城に戻しては
findings.governingReading: Kirei warns that sending Illya back to the castle would simply deliver her to Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English removes the custodial agency and makes the return Illya’s independent act.

findings.evidenceJa: お断りするわ
findings.governingReading: Illya completes the rapid three-way refusal pattern with her own emphatic rejection.
findings.explanation: The English turns the repeated comic formula into an apology.

findings.evidenceJa: 一人でやってく
findings.governingReading: Illya insists she can manage and carry on alone even without Berserker.
findings.explanation: “Do things myself” is vague and childish in a different way, losing the claim of self-sufficiency.

findings.evidenceJa: 嫌われたものね
findings.governingReading: Rin provocatively recasts Illya’s refusal as Shirou having made himself disliked.
findings.explanation: The English strengthens the maneuver into a direct assertion of continuing hatred.

findings.highlight: she doesn’t want to stay in that tiny house of yours
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方の家なんて狭苦しくて御免
findings.governingReading: Rin invents Illya saying Shirou’s house is oppressively cramped and beneath consideration.
findings.explanation: The English reduces cramped discomfort and emphatic rejection to small size and preference.

findings.highlight: I have to get away from Shirou
findings.evidenceJa: シロウから離れないといけない
findings.governingReading: Illya says she must keep her distance from Shirou for an unfinished reason.
findings.explanation: “Get away from” sounds like aversion or escape and primes Rin’s deliberately false hatred reading.

findings.evidenceJa: 実に冷淡にイリヤを責め立てる
findings.governingReading: Rin presses Illya with conspicuous coldness as part of a deliberate provocation.
findings.explanation: The English replaces forceful, cold interrogation with mild calm criticism, obscuring the maneuver.

findings.highlight: I never said I don’t want Shirou
findings.evidenceJa: シロウがイヤだなんて言ってない
findings.governingReading: Illya emphatically denies saying that she dislikes or cannot stand Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Don’t want Shirou” introduces possessive or romantic ambiguity.

findings.evidenceJa: ふふん、と穏やかに笑う
findings.governingReading: Rin gives a satisfied little “hmph” and smiles calmly after extracting Illya’s denial.
findings.explanation: “Gently” deletes the smug signal that exposes her successful tactic.

findings.highlight: whose house is Illya going to…?
findings.evidenceJa: 誰の家に行くことになったんだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou ends by wondering whose house Illya has actually ended up agreeing to stay at.
findings.explanation: The English trails off before completing the lodging question.
